title: A cooling cup of tea
caption: Newton's law of cooling gives T = 20 + 70e^(−kt): the tea starts at 90 °C and falls toward the 20 °C room. The reading 60 °C at 10 minutes fixes k = ln(70/40)/10 ≈ 0.056 per minute.
alt: A decaying curve starting at 90 degrees Celsius at time 0, passing through 60 degrees at 10 minutes and levelling off towards the dashed room-temperature line at 20 degrees.
description: The temperature starts at 90 °C and the room is at 20 °C.
The curve T = 20 + 70e^(−kt) falls fast at first, then more slowly.
The measurement 60 °C at 10 minutes gives k = ln(70/40)/10 ≈ 0.056 per minute.
The curve levels off at the room temperature, 20 °C.

checks.name: T(60) is close to the 20 °C room temperature
